shorts.hook: Forty-seven thousand aspen trunks in Utah are one single tree.
shorts.title: 47,000 Tree Trunks in Utah Are One Living Thing
shorts.outro: The fungus eating a whole forest is in the full video below.
shorts.description: Pando, a quaking aspen clone in Utah, is one root system under about 47,000 trunks, and mule deer are eating its young shoots; the fungus eating a whole forest is in the full episode.

shorts.hook: In Western Australia, a tree has been caught attacking underground phone cables.
shorts.title: This Christmas Tree Cuts Through Underground Phone Cables
shorts.outro: Doug's other five deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: Western Australia's Christmas tree, Nuytsia floribunda, clamps its roots onto anything it touches, buried telephone cables included; Doug's other deaths are in the full episode.

shorts.hook: The biggest fungus ever found covers nine hundred and sixty-five hectares.
shorts.title: The Biggest Fungus Ever Found Covers 1,350 Football Pitches
shorts.outro: Seven more hidden giants are in the full video below.
shorts.description: A single honey fungus in Oregon's Malheur National Forest covers 965 hectares and is at least 2,400 years old; the full episode on the forest it is killing is linked below.
